notes: Queue items are research prompts, not execution authority.
ISSUED means Director rendered the prompt for manual submission; it does not mean the external model received it.
Research artifacts are evidence inputs. Canonical or implementation changes require independent validation and existing AXIOM authority.
Do not enqueue raw sensitive/private operator context when a minimized research question is sufficient.

Automated R&D may select only `chatgpt` QUEUED items after the Director branch/PR write gate is current; manual-target items are never auto-rerouted, and automation output remains non-canonical until normal PR integration.

items.title: Long-horizon failure localization policy
items.question: How should a persistent autonomous agent choose checkpoint placement and failure-localization effort as task horizon, consequence, reversibility, and validator cost vary?
items.objective: Derive a falsifiable, implementation-relevant policy that minimizes root-to-detection wasted work while preserving validated completion.

items.title: Minimal temporal state semantics
items.question: What is the smallest temporal/supersession state model that captures most stale-fact and contradiction benefits for long-running agents without event-sourcing or graph-database complexity?
items.objective: Identify the minimum schema and transition semantics worth testing against AXIOM structured state.
constraints: do not assume bitemporal/event-sourced architecture is needed

items.title: Validated-work efficiency metric design
items.question: Which minimal telemetry schema and derived metrics best estimate validated useful work per unit of model, tool, latency, and human-attention cost?
items.objective: Produce a small provider-neutral metric set that can support routing research without Goodharting on token minimization.

items.title: Research artifact epistemic quality
items.question: How should an autonomous research pipeline score provenance, freshness, replication, benchmark validity, vendor conflicts, and unsupported precision before research becomes durable architectural input?
items.objective: Design a minimal evidence-quality contract that prevents model-generated research errors from recursively contaminating AXIOM.
constraints: no single scalar score unless justified

items.title: Context externalization and compaction
items.question: When can long-horizon agents safely remove reasoning/history after derived state is externalized, and what information must remain addressable to preserve recovery and auditability?
items.objective: Derive testable compaction rules that reduce context cost without losing constraints, causality, or recovery evidence.

items.title: Simple routing baselines under sparse evidence
items.question: Under low data volume and model/provider drift, which simple routing policies are hardest to beat and how should AXIOM decide that adaptive routing is not yet justified?
items.objective: Define a conservative routing benchmark and statistical promotion gate suitable for sparse AXIOM telemetry.

items.title: Destination-scoped agent egress capability
items.question: What is the smallest destination-aware network authorization contract that prevents unauthorized agent egress while remaining robust to redirects, DNS rebinding, private/link-local/metadata addresses, proxies, numeric IP forms, and dual-stack resolution?
items.objective: Specify a minimal egress capability and synthetic validation suite that can integrate with ASON/APEX without a broad architecture rewrite.

items.title: Minimal sequence-aware exfiltration policy
items.question: What is the smallest practical policy for blocking unsafe read-to-network and credential-to-network tool sequences without introducing a general-purpose taint-tracking system?
items.objective: Determine whether a compact data/effect classification and sequence rule materially improves AXIOM security over tool-level authorization alone.

items.title: Unauthorized inter-agent communication containment
items.question: How should an agent platform prevent shared caches, package proxies, artifacts, logs, or other infrastructure from becoming unauthorized inter-agent coordination channels?
items.objective: Derive minimal controls and tests for covert or accidental agent-to-agent communication through shared infrastructure.
constraints: do not prohibit legitimate coordination by default

items.title: Spoof-resistant tool result validation
items.question: How should persistent agents distinguish self-reported tool outputs, model-visible transcripts, execution receipts, and independently verified external outcomes so spoofed or fabricated tool results cannot become canonical state?
items.objective: Design the smallest evidence hierarchy and validation contract that prevents transcript-level tool-result spoofing from being accepted as execution truth.
constraints: reuse existing AXIOM receipts where possible

items.title: Agent credential discovery and least privilege
items.question: Which minimal credential-isolation, just-in-time access, and exposed-credential controls best prevent autonomous agents from discovering and reusing orphaned or overprivileged credentials?
items.objective: Identify implementable least-privilege patterns compatible with AXIOM's explicit authority and remote execution model.

items.title: Agentic MCP and tool supply-chain identity
items.question: What minimal identity/version binding should complement tool-schema digests so an agent can detect MCP or remote-tool implementation changes, endpoint substitution, and rug-pull behavior without requiring heavyweight attestation?
items.objective: Determine the smallest deployable control that closes material schema-only trust gaps for high-risk remote tools.

items.title: Machine-speed anomaly halt policy
items.question: Which low-complexity telemetry signals and stopping rules can detect and halt abnormal agent network/tool behavior at machine speed without excessive false shutdowns?
items.objective: Define a small anomaly-control baseline around destination novelty, request rate, denied actions, tool-chain patterns, and authorization drift.
constraints: no ML anomaly detector unless simple baselines fail

items.title: RAG indirect prompt injection boundary
items.question: Which structural separation and validation techniques measurably reduce indirect prompt-injection risk from retrieved documents without pretending untrusted natural-language content can be perfectly sanitized?
items.objective: Produce falsifiable RAG integrity tests and minimal boundary improvements for current AXIOM retrieval/generation flows.
constraints: no claim of perfect prompt-injection prevention
no tool authority from retrieved content

items.title: Defensive incident-analysis model readiness
items.question: How should a resource-constrained organization prepare reliable AI-assisted incident forensics when hosted models may refuse exploit-like defensive material or impose unsuitable data-boundary constraints?
items.objective: Define a minimal readiness strategy for defensive analysis without deploying unrestricted offensive capability or incurring unapproved hosted cost.
constraints: do not assume local workstation routing

items.title: Fully automated research-to-development control loop
items.question: What is the smallest safe architecture that can automate AXIOM research selection, evidence acquisition, Research-Manager reconciliation, candidate engineering, repository validation, and continuation while preserving explicit authority and preventing research output from self-authorizing code, merges, releases, spending, or external effects?
items.objective: Design an ASAP automation path that reuses the existing research queue and Director execution interfaces rather than creating a parallel R&D authority.
constraints: research-queue.json remains sole research work queue
$0 incremental hosted spend unless separately authorized
reuse existing Director/Harness/APEX/ASON controls where sufficient
